title: LeMela – Living with Melanoma: Testing an innovative care model (Phase B)
summary:
LeMela – Living with Melanoma is a feasibility study that evaluates a newly developed survivorship care programme at the skin cancer centers in Dresden and Halle (Saale), particularly taking into account the perspectives of patients, their families, and healthcare providers. The goal is to assess the feasibility of the LeMela programme and to evaluate the feasibility of a randomised controlled trial (RCT) on the programme’s outcomes.
A total of 200 patients (100 per site) with stage IIB–IV melanoma are expected to participate in the study; these patients have either already started or completed systemic therapy, or are currently undergoing such therapy. Study participants will be monitored over a period of 12 months. In this study, participants will be randomly assigned to two groups. One group will begin the programme immediately (intervention group). The other group will receive standard care at the skin cancer center (control group). The control group will also participate in the surveys. Participation in the study begins by completing a questionnaire. This is available online via the platform LimeSurvey. Alternatively, the questionnaire can also be provided in printed form. The questionnaire requires an email address so that follow-up questionnaires can be sent after 6 and 12 months. Completing the questionnaire takes approximately 35 minutes each time. The survey aims to assess the participants’ mental and physical well-being and how they seek, understand, and use health-related information (e.g., quality of life, health literacy). In addition, sociodemographic data (age, sex, socioeconomic status, living situation) will be collected, and participants will be asked to evaluate the questionnaire and the LeMela program. The LeMela program is a complex intervention that consists of five components: (1) program admission and screening for support needs, (2) a medical consultation with an individualised aftercare plan, (3) coordination of care by an oncology navigator, (4) counselling on information and support services, and (5) a training module on self-management and health literacy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with melanoma (ICD-10 C43, C69, C80 and mucosal melanomas; stages IIB–IV)
• Patients at the start of, during, and after completion of systemic therapy
• Sufficient cognitive and physical capacity to participate in the study
• Sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
• No declaration of consent (does not wish to or is unable to)
• insufficient knowledge of German
